title: Orrell station pedestrian access
author: Peter Whatley
licence: CC BY-SA 2.0 (read on the page, 11 October 2026)
kind: period (1989), a railway station's own approach, steel column
material: painted steel, pale yellow, with a short dark base sleeve (a stepped column)
what_it_shows: a slim tubular column with a dark base sleeve beside a paved ramp; the arm leaves the column top in one rounded bend and runs nearly level to a long canopy lantern lying in line with it
used: yes: bracket (one bend, near-level arm, lantern in line), the stepped base (variant A's sleeve), reach not measurable (no scale)

elements.bracket: one rounded bend of centreline radius about 3 tube diameters (the review's 130 is 3 diameters of 42: agrees), then a straight arm rising 8 degrees in the picture (read on a 5 x grid: 8 px over 55); true rake 0 to 10: the amended 0 +-5 agrees, 40 does not
elements.reach: the lantern's rear stands about 5 tube widths from the axis (20 px at 4 px of tube), 300 mm for a 60 top: shorter than 430; the scale is the tube's own unknown width, so it is listed (PW9), not amended
elements.lantern: a long boat-shaped canopy in line with the arm (within 5 degrees), about 14 top widths long (57 px), 850 mm for a 60 top: longer than 550; listed (PW12)
elements.shaft_taper: slim and parallel at this size, no taper readable
elements.base_door: a dark sleeve of 55 px in a column 290 px tall (about 0.19; read off the 640 px picture): A's 978 of 5000 is 0.2: agrees; no door visible
elements.root: the sleeve stands directly in the paving, no plate: agrees

title: Appley Bridge station
author: Peter Whatley
licence: CC BY-SA 2.0 (read on the page, 11 October 2026)
kind: period (1989), a railway platform's own lighting, steel column
material: painted steel, orange-red, with a black base sleeve about 0.3 of the column's visible height
what_it_shows: a stepped tubular column: a slim upper tube about 5 px wide steps out to about 7 px a third of the way down, a black sleeve at the foot, a rounded elbow at the top and a long pale canopy lantern lying on the arm; a station sign is masked grey in the crop
used: yes: bracket, base sleeve, lantern in line; paint colour is a railway's, not copied

elements.bracket: a rounded elbow of centreline radius about 2 tube diameters (read on a 6 x grid), then an arm of 14 px that is the lantern's own spigot length; the lantern's top edge rises 11 degrees in the picture (12 px over 60): true rake 0 to 10; the lantern is in line within 5 degrees
elements.reach: the lantern's rear stands about 2.8 tube widths from the axis (14 px at 5 px): 170 mm for a 60 top, 250 for an 89 top: much shorter than 430; listed (PW9), not amended (the scale is the unknown tube width)
elements.lantern: a long canopy about 12 top widths long (60 px): 720 mm for a 60 top; longer than 550; listed (PW12)
elements.shaft_taper: a visible STEP in the tube's diameter (5 px to 7 px), not a taper: a stepped column as BGE and US01 show (A's cone is such a step)
elements.base_door: a black sleeve of about 75 px in a column about 322 px tall (0.23): A's 0.2 agrees; no door visible; the step in the tube above it is a second change of diameter
elements.root: stands in a gravel and ash surface: no plate

title: Old rare lamp post on Shakespeare Road, Birchington
author: Robert Lamb
licence: CC BY-SA 2.0 (read on the page, 11 October 2026)
kind: later photograph of an object the photographer calls old and rare: a precast concrete column with its original 1960s lantern and an anti-glare shield (not a replacement by his word: 'an old lantern ... mounted upon a concrete column'); a mid-1960s to 1970s fitting that stood in 1990 and is not modern replacement stock
material: precast concrete column, painted steel bracket and lantern
what_it_shows: a concrete column rising to a mitred elbow, a straight arm and a long canopy lantern lying in line with it; an anti-glare plate hangs down at the lantern's rear
used: yes: bracket (an angular elbow, arm and lantern in line), the shaft's top width, lantern length; the lamp type (sodium or not) is not stated

elements.bracket: a mitred elbow, centreline radius about 55 (+-30; one diameter); the arm climbs 19 degrees in a picture taken looking up about 35 degrees, which a level arm pointing partly toward the camera shows: true rake 0 to 10; the lantern lies in line within 5 degrees: agrees with the amended 90 degree bend and level arm (the radius 130 is looser than this elbow: PW11)
elements.reach: the lantern's rear stands about 4.3 shaft-top widths from the axis, 430 to 540 for a top of 100 to 125: agrees with 430
elements.lantern: about seven column-top widths long (700 to 875 for a top of 100 to 125): longer than 550; listed, not amended
elements.shaft_taper: the shaft is about 10 px wide at the top and 13 px a third of the way down in a picture looking up: a foot about 1.7 to 2 times the top (looking up inflates it), agrees with 220 over 125 (1.76)
elements.base_door: a small pale plate low on the shaft, unreadable: the door is not seen
elements.root: the foot is out of frame

title: Lovely old 1950s/60s streetlight on Chigwell Road
author: Robert Lamb
licence: CC BY-SA 2.0 (read on the page, 11 October 2026)
kind: later photograph of an object unchanged since the period by the photographer's word: 'vintage 1950s/60s concrete lampposts ... one of many that still retains its original low pressure sodium lamp'; the only reached photograph that names a low-pressure sodium lamp on a concrete column
material: precast concrete column with a steel arm
what_it_shows: a slim concrete column with a curved gooseneck arm and a small lantern at its end, dusk, a bus stop sign at its foot
used: yes, as the disagreement: a curved arm, not an angular one; the column is slim and tapers little over the visible height

elements.bracket: a smooth curve (gooseneck), not a level arm: DISAGREES with the amended angular bracket; recorded as PW10, not written out (no number readable)
elements.reach: the lantern's centre stands about 5 shaft-top widths out
elements.lantern: small and set across the arm's end: a different, earlier pattern
elements.shaft_taper: slim at the top, no readable taper

title: Rosslyn Avenue, Coundon
author: John Brightley
licence: CC BY-SA 2.0 (read on the page, 11 October 2026)
kind: later photograph of an old precast pattern that stood in 1990 ('a style of concrete lamp post that has been replaced in many other locations because of the risk of concrete failure': this one is a survivor, so unchanged); a suburban street; the lantern's age is not stated
material: precast concrete column with a hooked steel top
what_it_shows: a tall slim concrete column, a hooked bracket curling over to a downward-facing lantern; pavement and kerb at its foot
used: yes, as a disagreement and for the proportions: the shaft tapers visibly from foot to top; the foot stands on the pavement with no plate

elements.bracket: a hook curving over, not a level arm: DISAGREES, PW10
elements.reach: about 3 shaft-top widths from the axis to the lantern's centre
elements.lantern: a small pot-shaped lantern on a hook: another pattern
elements.shaft_taper: a straight taper read on ten rows: 8 px across at the top (y 100), 9 at y 130, 10 at y 200, 11 at y 250 and 13 near the foot (y 400): a foot 1.6 times the top (the target's 220 over 125 is 1.76): agrees within the reading
elements.base_door: a plain square foot, no visible door at this size
elements.root: planted straight into the pavement, no plate or collar: agrees
